{{Short description|School mathematics competition in the Philippines}}
The '''Philippine Mathematical Olympiad''' is a [[secondary school]] [[mathematics competition]] among secondary school students.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PMO: Philippine Mathematical Olympiad {{!}} The Oldest and Most Prestigious Secondary Math Contest in the Philippines |url=https://pmo.ph |access-date=2024-10-01 |language=en-US}}</ref> First held in 1984, the PMO was created as a venue for high school students with interest and talent in [[mathematics]] to compete in a very hard contest.

It is the oldest and the most prominent nationwide mathematics competition among secondary school students in the [[Philippines]]. It is regarded as the first step to representing their country at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (IMO). It has three stages: two regional and one national.<ref name="GMA">{{cite news |last=Marchadesch  |first=Barbara |title= Philippine Math Olympiad winners gun for int'l honors |url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/scitech/science/247577/philippine-math-olympiad-winners-gun-for-int-l-honors/story/ |website=GMA News Online |access-date=2025-05-08}}</ref>

The [[Mathematical Society of the Philippines]] (MSP) selects a team from the top 20 PMO national finalists to represent the Philippines at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad|IMO]]. The Philippines first participated in the IMO in 1988.

==Winners==
Some PMO winners include:

* Andres Rico Gonzales III:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gonzales wins gold in 2017 China Southeast Mathematical Olympiad |url=https://www.letran.edu.ph/Colegio/ReadMore/1117 |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=letran.edu.ph}}</ref> Highest country rank in 2020
* Albert John Patupat:<ref>{{Cite web |title=International Mathematical Olympiad |url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=26055 |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=imo-official.org}}</ref> Highest country rank in 2018 
* Farrell Eldrian Wu, a naturalized Filipino,<ref>{{Cite web |title=AN ACT GRANTING PHILIPPINE CITIZENSHIP TO FARRELL ELDRIAN WU |url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/63752}}</ref> Highest country rank in 2016
** Incidentally, Farrell graduated in [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] with a perfect GPA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Filipino student graduates with perfect GPA at Massachusetts Institute of Technology |url=https://www.magzter.com/stories/Newspaper/Manila-Bulletin/Filipino-student-graduates-with-perfect-GPA-at-Massachusetts-Institute-of-Technology |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=magzter.com |language=en}}</ref>
